name: Casting Lots
overview: Casting lots was a divinely ordained practice used in the Old Testament to make important decisions and determine God's will, as seen when Aaron cast lots to designate the scapegoat (Leviticus 16:8) and when Joshua divided the land among Israel's tribes by casting lots before the Lord (Joshua 18:10; Numbers 26:55). This method was also employed in communal worship, such as allocating the wood offering among priests and Levites (Nehemiah 10:34), and even in the unfolding of providential events, illustrated by Haman casting lots to determine the timing of his decree (Esther 3:7). Additionally, casting lots symbolized the fulfillment of messianic prophecy, as the soldiers cast lots for Jesus’ garments (Psalms 22:18), demonstrating God's sovereign control over all circumstances.
